We were named "RevOps Platform of the Year" and no, we are not playing it cool about this one.

The MarTech Breakthrough Awards picked us out of thousands of nominations, from 15+ countries. We're still a little stunned, honestly.

Here's the part that actually matters:
Most revenue teams don't have a data problem. They have an agreement problem.
→ Marketing's looking at engagement signals
→ Sales is looking at CRM activity
→ Nobody's looking at the whole account

Which is exactly how you end up with sellers chasing the wrong deals, campaigns hitting the wrong stage, and a forecast that falls apart the second someone asks a follow-up question.

We fix that. One set of signals. One source of truth. For every human (and AI agent) doing the work.

Turns out when everyone's finally looking at the same intelligence, "trust the forecast" stops being the joke of every sales call.

And to our customers: you're the ones turning these ideas into real results every day. This award belongs to you, too.

postedAt.postedAgoText: 1 week ago • Visible to anyone on or off LinkedIn

posts.content:
Years ago, long before 6sense, I had one of those moments as a marketing leader that totally deflates you.  

Our pipeline numbers were incredible. I felt like we were crushing it. 

Included in that pipeline were three accounts that looked white-hot. All of them showed heavy buying signals and were in our ICP. Everything looked like the textbook definition of "ready to engage." 

I walked into my meeting with the sales team feeling great about what we had built. 

But then a rep asked, "Wait, why are we chasing these?" 

So I pulled up the data, showed him the signals, the research, the intent. 

He was completely unimpressed. "Yeah, but those accounts aren't going anywhere." 

Turns out, two of those three accounts were kicking tires because they were under budget pressure, not because they had a problem to solve. The third had a champion who was leaving in 30 days.  

How had we not caught that? Why were we so wrong? 

Turns out our signals were real. So was the research. What was missing was the context. 

The question has to go beyond, "Are they looking?"  

We have to ask:  

> Why are they looking?  
> What does that mean for how they'll buy?  
> Who has to believe in this before they take action? 

That’s the intelligence beneath the signals, and that’s what my team and I were missing. It’s what 6sense works obsessively to change. 

At Breakthrough 2026, we’ll show how we’re making sure the context shows up when and where it’s needed.  

Because no one wants that deflated “how did we get this so wrong?” feeling. We want to build pipeline we can trust and act on.

posts.content:
I've always believed a leader's real job is to make themselves obsolete. 

Not because your work doesn't matter. Because if you've done it right, the company no longer needs you the way it once did. That your departure at some point should become a non-event.  

Three weeks ago, I informed the company that I made the decision to step down as CEO of 6sense in mid-September and hand the reins to our COO Amir Ravandoust. 

I have watched Amir operate over the past 14 months. Shoulder to shoulder, he and I, alongside this team, have built a strategy we believe is the right one for this Agentic GTM era, have assembled an exceptional executive team, and rebuilt a culture that's become genuinely ours, not mine. That work is real, and it's exactly what gives me the confidence to step back now, at a moment when our team, our strategy, and our board are fully aligned. 

This next chapter calls for deep, hands-on operational execution. I believe Amir is uniquely qualified to lead it. He knows our business and our technology as well as anyone here and is fully committed to the strategy and plan we've built together. And most importunately, I have seen his true character and how we cares about people. I am honored to call him a friend. Our direction isn't changing — it's really the same plan, led by Amir and this executive team that I believe in fully. 

Making yourself obsolete isn't a moment of loss. It's the clearest sign that what you have built matters. 

Grateful beyond words to this team, and excited to watch what comes next.

posts.content:
Our BDRs are crushing it! I get so many questions from CMOs asking me if we are replacing BDRs with AI, and I respond with an enthusiastic NO! The BDRs at 6sense are currently driving 64% of our pipeline, and I am not about to rock that boat. They are simply the lifeblood of our new business motion. 

Don’t get me wrong. We are using AI to automate sequences, respond to inbound inquiries, help with event follow-up, auto dial, etc, but the human outreach is so impactful for connecting and converting. 

I had the privilege of spending the day in our New York office today, meeting 1-on-1 with all 10 rockstars on our BDR East team. They were motivated, encouraged, optimistic, and so grateful to work together. It was infectious. 

The BDR role is such a stepping stone to every other GTM function that the experience is priceless. Some of our BDRs want to be AEs next, some want to do MOPs, some field marketing or ABX, some want to be BDR managers or directors, some are exploring the SC or CSM route. All of those paths are viable! That’s what makes this role so important for building your GTM talent pipeline. 

Huge shout out to the NY BDR East team… Jackson Boro, Ray Dearth, Sarah Oberman, Daniel Boyajian, Sydney Vaupell, Christiana Pisani, Noah Gitta, Lilah Blackburn, Christopher Salatto, and their fearless and passionate leader Nicholas Rosimini.

posts.content:
One thing I've learned building AI products: "trust" is not a feature you ship. It's something you earn through consistency and clarity. 

An agent that's confident is not worth much unless it’s also grounded in truth. That means it has access to verified data, knows where its signals come from, can trace back why it's making a recommendation. 

The foundation matters. A lot. You can have the most sophisticated agent in the world, but if it's working from fragmented people data, incomplete contact lists, or signal streams you can't verify, you're still guessing, but now it’s at scale. 

This is why we spend so much time on the unglamorous part: making sure the intelligence layer is solid:  

> Better people data 

> Verified decision-makers 

> Executive identification you can trust 

> Every contact, every signal, rooted in something real 

When that foundation is there, your tools stop being shiny and start being valuable. 

When your agents have access to defensible, explainable intelligence — the kind that comes from 13 years of building this deliberately — they move from interesting experiments to engines that drive pipeline. 

We just made that foundation available programmatically and directly inside the agents your teams use every day. Because intelligence your teams trust is intelligence they'll act on.
